member.name: M:SharpVectors.Renderers.Texts.WpfTextRenderer.MapNumericFontWeightToStandard(System.Int32)
member.summary: Maps a numeric font-weight value to the nearest standard CSS font-weight.

remarks.para: Specification: CSS Font Module Level 3 and 4
Standard Weights: 100, 200, 300, 400 (Normal), 500, 600 (SemiBold), 700 (Bold), 800 (ExtraBold), 900 (Black), 950 (UltraBlack)

item.description: Non-standard numeric values are rounded to the nearest standard weight using Euclidean distance.
Example: 650 → nearest is 700 (distance 50) vs 600 (distance 50), but 700 wins due to index ordering.
Example: 550 → 500 or 600 are equidistant; 500 is returned as the first match.

remarks.para: Debug Output: Emits Debug.WriteLine messages when clamping or rounding is applied, enabling runtime diagnostics without performance overhead in Release builds.

member.param: A CSS numeric font-weight value (typically 100–950).
member.returns: The nearest standard from the CSS specification.

member.name: M:SharpVectors.Renderers.Texts.WpfTextRenderer.GetTextFontWeight(System.String)
member.summary: Resolves a CSS font-weight string to a WPF .
member.remarks:
Supported Input Formats:
CSS Keywords: "normal", "bold"
Numeric Values: "100", "200", ..., "900", "950"
Non-standard Numeric: Any integer; rounded to nearest standard weight via .
Null/Empty: Defaults to "normal" (400).
Non-Standard Numeric Behavior: When a numeric font-weight is provided that does not correspond to a standard CSS weight (e.g., 650, 475, 550), the value is rounded to the nearest standard weight. This ensures compatibility with WPF's standard FontWeight values while preserving the user's intent. See for detailed rounding examples.
member.param: A CSS font-weight string (e.g., "bold", "700", "650").
member.returns: A WPF corresponding to the input; defaults to Normal if parsing fails.

member.name: M:SharpVectors.Renderers.Texts.WpfTextRenderer.GetTextFontWeight(SharpVectors.Dom.Svg.SvgTextContentElement)
member.summary: Resolves the font-weight property of an SVG text element, with support for relative keywords and parent-relative adjustments.
member.remarks:
Priority Order:
Direct CSS keywords: "normal", "bold"
Direct numeric values: "100"–"950"
Relative keywords with parent lookup: "bolder", "lighter"
Fallback: "normal" (400) if no valid value is found
Relative Keywords:
"bolder": Looks up the parent element's font-weight and applies one step heavier (via ). If no parent or parent weight unavailable, defaults to ExtraBold (800).
"lighter": Looks up the parent element's font-weight and applies one step lighter (via ). If no parent or parent weight unavailable, defaults to Light (300).
Non-Standard Numeric Handling: Non-standard numeric values are automatically rounded via . This ensures smooth rendering across both CSS and WPF specifications.
member.param: The SVG text element from which to extract the font-weight property.
member.returns: The resolved ; defaults to Normal if no value is specified or parsing fails.

member.name: M:SharpVectors.Renderers.Texts.WpfTextRenderer.GetBolderFontWeight(System.String)
member.summary: Resolves one step heavier font-weight from a given parent font-weight value.

remarks.para: Specification: CSS Font Module Level 3, Section 3.3 (font-weight)
This method implements the "bolder" keyword semantics, moving from the current weight up one step in the CSS weight hierarchy:

member.name: T:SharpVectors.Renderers.Wpf.CssVariableResolver
member.summary: Resolves CSS custom property (variable) references with support for fallbacks, nested variables, and fallback chains.
member.remarks:
Specification: CSS Cascading Variables Module Level 1 (css-variables-1)
Purpose: This resolver robustly handles CSS var() function calls that may be unresolved at render time. It supports fallback extraction, nested variables, fallback chains, and cycle detection.
Supported Patterns:
Simple: "var(--my-color)" → empty (unresolved)
With fallback: "var(--my-color, #FF0000)" → "#FF0000"
Nested fallback: "var(--missing, var(--also-missing, #000))" → "#000" (recursive resolution)
Multiple vars: "var(--a) var(--b, #111)" → processed independently
Whitespace handling: "var( --name , fallback )" → normalized
Edge Cases Handled:
Circular references: Tracked via depth limit and visited set to prevent infinite recursion
Unresolved chains: Falls back to empty string if no terminal value found
Malformed syntax: Treated as non-variable, returned unchanged

member.name: F:SharpVectors.Renderers.Wpf.CssVariableResolver.MaxRecursionDepth
member.summary: Maximum recursion depth for variable fallback chains (e.g., var(--a, var(--b, var(--c, ...)))). Prevents stack overflow from circular references or pathological nesting.

member.name: M:SharpVectors.Renderers.Wpf.CssVariableResolver.ResolveVariables(System.String)
member.summary: Resolves CSS variable references in a property value with support for fallbacks and nested variables.
member.remarks:
This is the main entry point for CSS variable resolution. It handles: - Simple unresolved variables: "var(--missing)" → "" (empty, triggers default) - Variables with fallback: "var(--missing, #FF0000)" → "#FF0000" - Nested/chained fallbacks: "var(--a, var(--b, #000))" → "#000" - Multiple var() in one value: Each is processed independently
Non-variable strings (e.g., "red", "#000", "300") are returned unchanged.
member.param: A CSS property value that may contain var() function syntax.
member.returns: A resolved value, fallback value, or empty string if unresolved.

member.name: T:SharpVectors.Renderers.Wpf.WpfPaintOrder
member.summary: Represents the SVG paint-order CSS property value. Specifies the order in which fill, stroke, and markers are rendered on an element.

remarks.para: The paint-order property allows you to change the rendering order of fill, stroke, and markers. By default (Normal), fill is drawn first, then stroke (which appears on top), then markers.
This is particularly useful for: - Icons with visible outlines/strokes - Text with colored outlines - Graphics where the stroke should be the primary visual
Reference: https://www.w3.org/TR/svg2/painting.html#PaintOrder

member.name: F:SharpVectors.Renderers.Wpf.WpfPaintOrder.Normal
member.summary: Default: fill, stroke, markers Fill is drawn first, stroke appears on top (WPF default behavior)

member.name: F:SharpVectors.Renderers.Wpf.WpfPaintOrder.Stroke
member.summary: Stroke first: stroke, fill, markers Stroke is drawn first, fill appears on top This creates the effect of an outline with a colored interior

member.name: F:SharpVectors.Renderers.Wpf.WpfPaintOrder.Fill
member.summary: Fill explicit: fill, stroke, markers Explicit specification of fill-first order (same as Normal)

member.name: F:SharpVectors.Renderers.Wpf.WpfPaintOrder.Markers
member.summary: Markers first: markers, stroke, fill Markers are drawn first (for future enhanced marker support)

member.name: T:SharpVectors.Renderers.Wpf.WpfPaintOrderHelper
member.summary: Helper class for parsing and handling the paint-order CSS property

member.name: M:SharpVectors.Renderers.Wpf.WpfPaintOrderHelper.Parse(System.String)
member.summary: Parse a paint-order CSS value string to the corresponding enum value
member.param: The CSS paint-order value to parse. Can be null, empty, whitespace, or one of: "normal", "stroke", "fill", "markers" Can also be space-separated keywords like "stroke fill", "markers stroke fill", etc.
member.returns: The corresponding WpfPaintOrder enum value. Returns Normal if the value is null, empty, or unrecognized. Parsing is case-insensitive.

remarks.para: Phase 2 Implementation (Enhanced): Now supports multi-keyword paint-order values. The first keyword in the sequence determines the rendering behavior: - "stroke fill" → interpreted as Stroke (stroke-first order) - "fill stroke" → interpreted as Fill (fill-first order) - "markers stroke fill" → interpreted as Markers (markers-first order, Phase 3+)
Subsequent keywords are reserved for future phases that may support more granular multi-order rendering control.
